title: Are Too Many Americans Taking Antidepressants? - Nautilus
gist: A psychiatrist of 35-plus years weighs the claim that Americans are overprescribed antidepressants — now taken by 1 in 6 adults — against HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s May 2026 push for alternatives, concluding there are grains of truth to the overuse case but a far more nuanced full picture.

insights.claim: Drugs for treating depression are among the most prescribed category of medications in the U.S., with 1 in 6 American adults taking them.
insights.so_what: A roughly 17 percent adult penetration rate means even a modest policy-driven decline in initiation would be a material volume event for the category.
insights.locator: Drugs for treating depression are among the most prescribed
insights.speaker: Andrew McLean

insights.claim: Rates of anxiety and depression have grown since the COVID-19 pandemic, and so have prescriptions for antidepressants.
insights.so_what: Post-pandemic prescription growth is the demand backdrop that any policy push against antidepressants is fighting against.
insights.quote: Rates of anxiety and depression have grown since the COVID-19 pandemic—as have prescriptions for antidepressants
insights.locator: Are Too Many Americans Taking Antidepressants?
insights.speaker: Andrew McLean

insights.claim: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. launched an effort in May 2026 encouraging doctors to find ways other than antidepressants and other psychiatric drugs to treat depression where possible.
insights.so_what: Federal prescribing pressure is now explicit policy, not advocacy — a concrete regulatory risk to psychiatric drug volumes and a tailwind for non-pharmacological alternatives.
insights.quote: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who launched an effort in May 2026 encouraging doctors to find other ways besides antidepressants and other psychiatric drugs to treat depression when possible
insights.locator: Some health researchers and advocates have raised concerns
insights.speaker: Andrew McLean

insights.claim: A distinct strand of the criticism is not over-prescribing but discontinuation: critics say patients who want to stop taking antidepressants struggle to do so.
insights.so_what: Difficulty stopping is a stickiness feature for revenue and a liability exposure at the same time — watch tapering protocols and any litigation around withdrawal.
insights.quote: too many patients are using antidepressants and that patients who want to stop taking them struggle to do so
insights.locator: Some health researchers and advocates have raised concerns
insights.speaker: Andrew McLean

insights.claim: A psychiatrist of more than 35 years, formerly medical director of North Dakota’s Department of Human Services, concludes there are grains of truth to claims that antidepressants are overused but that the full picture is much more nuanced.
entities: North Dakota Department of Human Services
insights.so_what: The clinical middle ground argues against an abrupt volume collapse; expect policy friction at the margin of new initiations rather than mass discontinuation.
insights.quote: there are grains of truth to claims that they are overused, but the full picture is much more nuanced
insights.locator: As a psychiatrist for over 35 years
insights.speaker: Andrew McLean
